data.name: Heading
data.comment: The heading of the Timing panel: how fast the photos play, so how long the video is. Keep it to about 14 characters: it is also a tab in a narrow window, beside Frame and Output.

data.name: ModesName
data.comment: The screen reader name of the three-part switch that picks how the speed is set (Per second, Length, Per photo).

data.name: ModePerSecond
data.comment: The first part of the speed switch: set how many photos play per second (frames per second). Keep it to about 11 characters: the three parts share the 280 px row equally (about 93 px each); longer text ends in an ellipsis.

data.name: ModeLength
data.comment: The second part of the speed switch: set how long the whole video lasts, a duration in time (not a distance). Keep it to about 11 characters.

data.name: ModePerPhoto
data.comment: The third part of the speed switch: set how many seconds each photo stays on screen. Keep it to about 11 characters.

data.name: PresetsFramesPerSecond
data.comment: The screen reader name of the row of preset rates (12 to 60) in Per second mode.

data.name: PresetsLength
data.comment: The screen reader name of the row of preset lengths (10 s to 60 s) in Length mode.

data.name: PresetsSecondsPerPhoto
data.comment: The screen reader name of the row of preset times per photo (0.25 s to 5 s) in Per photo mode.

data.name: CustomFramesPerSecond
data.comment: The caption over the box for a rate of one's own in Per second mode; also the box's screen reader name.

data.name: CustomLength
data.comment: The caption over the box for a video length of one's own (a duration) in Length mode; also the box's screen reader name.

data.name: CustomSecondsPerPhoto
data.comment: The caption over the box for a time per photo of one's own in Per photo mode; also the box's screen reader name.

data.name: UnitSecondsPerPhoto
data.comment: The unit after the box in Per photo mode. Use the same words as CoreText.SecondsPerPhotoFormat without its number. Keep it to about 16 characters.

data.name: NotANumberFramesPerSecond
data.value: Type a frame rate from {0} to {1} fps, like 24 or {2}.
data.comment: Under the box when what was typed in Per second mode is not a number. {0} the lowest rate ("1"), {1} the highest ("120"), {2} an NTSC rate as example ("29.97"). Use the abbreviation of CoreText.FramesPerSecond.

data.name: NotANumberLength
data.value: Type a length in seconds, like 30, or as minutes and seconds, like 1:30. It can be from {0} to {1}.
data.comment: Under the box when what was typed in Length mode is not a length. {0} the shortest length ("0.1 s"), {1} the longest ("10 h 00 min"). "1:30" is typed with a colon whatever the language.

data.name: NotANumberSecondsPerPhoto
data.value: Type how many seconds each photo stays, from {0} to {1}.
data.comment: Under the box when what was typed in Per photo mode is not a number. {0} the shortest time ("0.01 s"), {1} the longest ("10 s").

data.name: ClampedFramesPerSecond
data.value: Frame rates run from {2} to {3} fps, so {0} is now {1}.
data.comment: Under the box when a rate outside the range was typed. {0} what was typed, as typed ("200"), {1} the rate now set ("120 fps"), {2} the lowest ("1"), {3} the highest ("120").

data.name: ClampedLength
data.value: A video can be from {2} to {3} long, so {0} is now {1}.
data.comment: Under the box when a length outside the range was typed. {0} what was typed, as typed, {1} the length now set ("0.1 s"), {2} the shortest ("0.1 s"), {3} the longest ("10 h 00 min").

data.name: ClampedSecondsPerPhoto
data.value: A photo can stay from {2} to {3}, so {0} is now {1}.
data.comment: Under the box when a time per photo outside the range was typed. {0} what was typed, as typed, {1} the time now set ("10 s"), {2} the shortest, {3} the longest.

data.name: NtscRate
data.comment: Under the box when a typed rate became the exact rate of the NTSC video standard. {0} the rate ("29.97 fps"), {1} and {2} the exact fraction ("30000", "1001"; keep the slash).

data.name: ThousandsSeparator
data.value: Type 1000 without a separator, or {0} for one and a half.
data.comment: Under the box when "1,000" or "1.000" was typed: it is refused rather than guessed. {0} one and a half written with your decimal separator ("1.5", "1,5"). Keep "1000" as digits.

data.name: Rounded
data.comment: Under the box when more decimals were typed than it keeps. {0} the value kept, with its unit ("37.48 fps").

data.name: LengthTooShort
data.value: Your photos can't play in {0}: the fastest speed is {1}, so the video is {2} long.
data.comment: Length mode, when the photos cannot play in the chosen length even at the fastest speed. {0} the chosen length ("30 s"), {1} the fastest speed ("120 fps"), {2} the length the video has instead ("41.7 s").

data.name: LengthTooLong
data.value: Your photos can't fill {0}: the slowest speed is {1}, so the video is {2} long.
data.comment: Length mode, when the photos cannot fill the chosen length even at the slowest speed. {0} the chosen length, {1} the slowest speed ("10 s per photo"), {2} the length the video has instead.

data.name: DirectionName
data.comment: The caption over the switch between Forward and Boomerang in the Timing panel; also the switch's screen reader name. Keep it short (a caption).

data.name: DirectionForward
data.comment: The first part of the direction switch: the photos play forward, as usual. Keep it to about 11 characters: the two parts share the 280 px row equally; longer text ends in an ellipsis.

data.name: DirectionBoomerang
data.comment: The second part of the direction switch: the photos play forward, then backward to the first one (a boomerang loop). Keep it to about 11 characters.

data.name: PlaysName
data.comment: The caption over the row of numbers 1 to 5: how many times the photos play one after the other in the video; also the row's screen reader name.

data.name: PlaysGif
data.value: A GIF loops by itself, so it plays your photos once.
data.comment: In place of the numbers 1 to 5 while the output is an animated GIF: a GIF repeats forever on its own, so the photos are in it once.

data.name: HoldStart
data.comment: The caption over the box for how many seconds the first frame stays on screen before the photos play; also the box's screen reader name. A hold is a freeze frame: use your language's video-editing term for it (German Standbild, French arrêt sur image, Italian fermo immagine), never the Pause button's word, which sits next to it in the player. Keep it short (two boxes share the row; it may wrap to two lines).

data.name: HoldEnd
data.comment: The caption over the box for how many seconds the last frame stays on screen after the photos played. The same freeze-frame term as Hold at start. Keep it short.

data.name: NotANumberHold
data.value: Type a hold in seconds, like {2}. It can be from {0} to {1}.
data.comment: Under the hold boxes when what was typed is not a number of seconds. {0} the shortest hold ("0 s"), {1} the longest ("10 s"), {2} one and a half written with your decimal separator ("1.5").

data.name: ClampedHold
data.value: A hold can be from {2} to {3}, so {0} is now {1}.
data.comment: Under the hold boxes when a hold past the range was typed. {0} what was typed, as typed, {1} the hold now set ("10 s"), {2} the shortest ("0 s"), {3} the longest ("10 s").

data.name: HoldLasts
data.comment: Under a hold box when, at the video's speed, the hold lasts another length than the box shows: a hold is a whole number of the video's frames, at least one (at 2 s per photo, 0.3 s lasts one 2 s frame). {0} the length it lasts ("2.0 s"). Half a row wide; it may wrap.

data.name: LengthHoldsTooLong
data.value: The holds alone fill {0} (they last {1}): shorten them to make room for your photos. The video is {2} long.
data.comment: Length mode, when the holds at the start and the end together last as long as the chosen length or longer, so no speed lets the photos fit. {0} the chosen length ("5 s"), {1} the two holds together ("20 s"), {2} the length the video has instead. A hold is a freeze frame: use the word of the Hold at start and Hold at end boxes, not the Pause button's.

data.name: ThousandsSeparatorHold
data.value: Type the hold with one decimal at most, from {0} to {1}, like {2}.
data.comment: Under the hold boxes when what was typed has a separator and three digits ("2.500", "1,000"), which could be a thousands separator or a decimal point. {0} the shortest hold ("0 s"), {1} the longest ("10 s"), {2} one and a half written with your decimal separator ("1.5"). A hold is a freeze frame: use the word of the Hold at start and Hold at end boxes.
